newsitem.title: USA: Grace OKs unit's merger to Fresenius.
newsitem.headline: Grace OKs unit's merger to Fresenius.

text.p: W.R. Grace & Co said on Monday that its shareholders approved the $4.4 billion plan to merge its National Medical Care Inc dialysis unit with Fresenius AG, forming the world's largest integrated dialysis company.
Grace said it will now focus on its packaging and specialty chemicals units with $3.3 billion in annual sales.

When the deal is completed, Grace shareholders will receive 44.8 percent of Fresenius Medical Care AG, the name of the combined dialysis businesses, and 100 percent of the packaging and specialty chemicals business.
Grace said the transactions are expected to be completed by the end of the month.

Albert Costello, the chairman, president and chief executive of W.R. Grace, said in a statement, "The tax-free transaction approved today is valued by the Street at more than $4.4 billion, a value considerably above all other proposals received."
Baxter International Inc had proposed an acquisition of Grace's dialysis business earlier this year.

For each Grace common share, shareholders will receive one share of the "new" Grace; one share of a new class of preferred stock based solely on the five-year cash flow of Fresenius Medical Care AG; and approximately 1.013 American Depositary Shares (ADS) of Fresenius Medical Care.

Each ADS represents one third of an ordinary share of Fresenius Medical Care AG and has a current market value of more than $22, based on the value of Fresenius USA Inc combined with National Medical.
Grace said it will receive a cash distribution of approximately $2.3 billion from National Medical Care prior to closing, which is expected at the end of the month.

Grace said approximately $1 billion of the distribution will be used to repurchase stock, and the remainder will be applied to reducing debt and to investment in Grace's packaging and specialty chemicals businesses, the company said.

Grace said it intends to resume purchases of its stock under a previously authorized 10 million share repurchase program, leading to the repurchase of up to 20 percent of the company's outstanding common stock.
Fresenius AG shareholders approved the transaction last April. Shareholders of Fresenius USA Inc, the U.S. subsidiary of Fresenius AG, also are voting on the transaction today, Grace said.
The "new" Grace and Fresenius Medical Care ADSs FMS.N are expected to begin trading on the New York Stock Exchange on a when-issued basis Tuesday, Grace said.
